title: mos.drive.v1
description: Static drive facts emitted by `mos drive --json`: what IS this drive, vs mos.metadata.v1's what disc is this (design: doc/research/2026-06-10-media-info-design.md and 2026-06-16-drive-identity-enrichment-survey.md). This is the verb where the user asks for the canonical truth, so identity (vendor/product/revision), version and version_descriptors are read FRESH from a raw standard INQUIRY, with the DiscRecording directory cache as fallback; capabilities/profiles/firmware_date are one GET CONFIGURATION RT=0 walk. The drive-disc JOIN is consumer-side: the pipeline that loaded a disc knows which drive it used. serial is the durable inventory key that survives replug and machine moves; registry_id is ATTACHMENT identity (replug mints a new one) and must not be used as a durable key.

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node of the current media, or null when the drive is empty. Addressing context — a drive property only while this disc is loaded.

registry_id.description: Drive service IORegistry entry ID — attachment identity, the state/event join key. 0 = unavailable. NOT durable: replug mints a new ID by construction.

vendor.description: Vendor identification. FRESH from this verb's raw standard INQUIRY (the canonical drive truth), falling back to the DiscRecording pre-parsed directory cache when the raw read can't run (BUSY/mounted); null when neither has it. Same sanitization rules as mos.state.v1. (Other verbs that don't issue the raw INQUIRY — list/state — use the DR cache.)

product.description: Product identification, same terms/source as vendor.

revision.description: Firmware revision (SPC-4 PRODUCT_REVISION_LEVEL) — the firmware VERSION (4 chars); the creation date is firmware_date. Same terms/source as vendor (fresh INQUIRY, DR fallback).

serial.description: INQUIRY unit serial (VPD page 0x80) — the durable drive-inventory key that survives replug and machine moves (registry_id is attachment identity, replug mints a new one). Read via a raw INQUIRY (EVPD=1, PAGE CODE=0x80): the convenience Inquiry issues only a standard INQUIRY, so the page is unreachable through it, satisfying the AGENTS layer-1 raw-verb showing (design: doc/research/2026-06-16-serial-vpd-0x80-feasibility.md). null when the drive is busy/mounted (the raw read backs off on exclusive access rather than contend), the drive does not implement the page, or no serial is programmed.

capabilities.description: Spec-grounded GET CONFIGURATION facts only — the same bits a MakeMKV drive dump shows as 'Highest AACS version' / bus-encryption flags, WITHOUT the LibreDrive status synthesis (a MakeMKV database property, not a drive property; mos emits no libredrive field by design).

aacs.description: AACS feature (0x010D) present in the feature list. false on every non-BD drive — data, not an error.

aacs_version.description: AACS Version (feature payload byte 3), null when aacs is false.

bus_encryption.description: DRIVE-REPORTED bus-encryption support (feature payload byte 0 bit 1, per libaacs/UDFclient agreement), null when aacs is false. A firmware assertion: the cryptographically signed BEC bit lives in the AACS drive certificate behind REPORT KEY, which mos does not issue (scope doctrine).

profiles.description: Supported-profile set from the GET CONFIGURATION Profile List feature (0x0000) — the drive-static disc types this drive handles (the modern, BD-aware capability set, superseding the legacy MODE SENSE page-0x2A read/write media bits). The per-descriptor Current bit is media-dependent and deliberately omitted; this is what the drive CAN do, irrespective of the loaded disc. Empty array when the feature was absent (data, not an error). A consumer matches a profile by its stable MMC code or its name; an unknown code carries name null and is identified by code.

code.description: MMC profile number as lowercase hex (e.g. 0x0008 CD-ROM, 0x0010 DVD-ROM, 0x002b DVD+R DL, 0x0043 BD-RE).

name.description: Lowercase profile name (mos_profile_name), or null for a code mos does not name (consumer falls back to code).

version.description: Standard INQUIRY VERSION byte (SPC compliance level), from a raw standard INQUIRY (EVPD=0). null when that read could not be performed (BUSY / mounted media) — the same exclusive-access self-gating as serial.

name.description: SPC-level token (mos_spc_version_name): spc / spc_2 … spc_5; null for 0 (none), legacy SCSI-1/2, or unknown (consumer uses code).

version_descriptors.description: The T10/ISO standards the drive claims, from the INQUIRY version descriptors (bytes 58-73 of standard INQUIRY data). Empty array when the standard INQUIRY was unreadable (BUSY) or the drive listed none. Each code is the stable 2-byte descriptor value; a consumer matches by code or name.

code.description: Version descriptor code, lowercase hex (e.g. 0x04e0 MMC-6, 0x0460 SPC-4).

name.description: Standard token (mos_version_descriptor_name) for the 'no version claimed' family codes; null for a specific-revision or non-listed code (consumer uses the hex code).

firmware_date.description: Firmware creation timestamp from the GET CONFIGURATION Firmware Information feature (010Ch; MMC-6 §5.3.43 Table 197 — Century/Year/Month/Day/Hour/Minute/Second decimal ASCII, GMT), on the same RT=0 walk that yields capabilities/profiles. SAME RFC 3339 UTC format as mos.event.v1's `ts` (integer seconds, trailing Z). null when the drive does not implement the feature (common). NOTE: this is the firmware's CREATION date, not a version string — the 4-char revision remains the firmware version identifier.

speeds.description: Read/write performance from GET PERFORMANCE (0xAC, Type 00h Performance Data) via the GetPerformance convenience method — the MMC-sanctioned modern speed source (the convenience signature exposes the WRITE bit but not the TYPE field, so write-speed descriptors are unreachable; read and write are two calls, WRITE=0/1). MEDIA-DEPENDENT: performance reflects the loaded medium, so this is null when no media is loaded or the drive reported no descriptors in either direction (zero is data, not error). Spec-derived descriptor layout (no in-repo capture yet); a real GET PERFORMANCE capture is a falsifier per the hardware ADR.

descriptor_count.description: Number of performance descriptors in the read-direction reply.

max_read_kbps.description: Maximum read performance (kB/s) across the WRITE=0 descriptors.

max_write_kbps.description: Maximum write performance (kB/s) across the WRITE=1 descriptors (0 on a read-only drive / non-writable medium).

mechanical.description: MODE SENSE(10) page 0x2A (MM Capabilities & Mechanical Status) via the ModeSense10 convenience method — the mechanical facts GET CONFIGURATION cannot carry: loading-mechanism type, eject/lock support, the live media-locked bit, and the drive buffer size. Read-only (no MODE SELECT). null when the command failed or page 0x2A was absent. loading_mechanism and eject are kernel-confirmed (sr.c get_capabilities); buffer_kb and the lock bits are the standard MMC-3 page-2A positions with no in-repo capture yet (hardware falsifier per the ADR).

loading_mechanism.description: Loading-mechanism token (page[6] bits 7:5 via mos_loading_mechanism_name), or null for a reserved/unknown code.

locked.description: Media is currently locked (page[6] bit 2) — the live state bit.

error_recovery.description: MODE SENSE(10) page 0x01 (Read/Write Error Recovery) via the ModeSense10 convenience method — the drive's read error-recovery configuration. Read-only: mos reports it, it never issues the MODE SELECT that recovery tools (dvdisaster, sdparm) use to tune it. null when the command failed or page 0x01 was absent.

allOf.title: aacs false forces null version and bus_encryption
allOf.description: Both fields decode from the AACS feature payload; without the feature there is nothing to report and false/0 would fabricate a reading.
